supported_claims.text: 口 is a pictograph of an open human mouth; the visible graph represents the physical mouth as a whole. Its early meaning is “mouth,” associated with speaking and eating.
The selected late Shang bronze-style image is a modern redraw associated with a named vessel. It illustrates an early mouth-like form but is not itself an artifact image.

The record tradition includes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal, and clerical forms. The available evidence supports these as examples of the graph’s history, but not a precise stroke-by-stroke sequence between them.

Later documented uses include an opening of an object and household population/counting. These are distinct uses of the graph; the evidence does not establish when they arose or a semantic chain connecting them to “mouth.”

limitations.text: The exact first attestation of 口 is not established; the cited oracle examples are indexed examples, not an independently verified date for the graph’s first use.

The underlying inscriptions and selected glyph images were not visually examined in this research pass. The chosen bronze example is a modern redraw, so fine graphic details and a detailed evolution sequence cannot be confirmed from it.
The cited texts document later uses for openings and population, but do not determine their earliest occurrences or prove semantic development from the mouth sense.
